claims.summary: For every pair of 32-bit inputs, the exported gcd function returns their unsigned greatest common divisor.
claims.statement:
∀ (a b : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Rust.Lifted.module "gcd" [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 a, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 b]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (BitVec.ofNat 32 (a.toNat.gcd b.toNat))]
claims.reason: The statement covers every pair of 32-bit inputs and returns their unsigned greatest common divisor, including gcd(a, 0) = a.
claims.name: Examples.Rust.gcd
claims.intent: `gcd(a, b)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: their greatest common divisor (`gcd(a, 0) = a`).
details: Covers every pair of 32-bit bit patterns passed as two i32 arguments; the inputs are interpreted as unsigned natural numbers when computing the greatest common divisor.
The returned i32 is the 32-bit wrapping representation of that greatest common divisor; since the gcd of two 32-bit unsigned values fits in 32 bits, this does not change its value.

Returns additionally guarantees that the module can be instantiated and that, for every host behavior and every fresh instance, the call terminates without trapping and returns exactly the specified value.

claims.summary: For every triple of 32-bit inputs, the exported clamp function applies the specified signed comparisons and returns the selected input.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Rust.Lifted.module "clamp"
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 hi]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (if x.slt lo = true then lo else if hi.slt x = true then hi else x)]
claims.reason: It uses signed comparisons and returns lo when x is below lo, hi when x is above hi, and x otherwise, matching the stated behavior for every input triple.
claims.name: Examples.Rust.clamp
claims.intent: `clamp(x, lo, hi)` on signed 32-bit ints: `lo` below `lo`, `hi` above `hi`, else `x`.
details: Covers every triple of 32-bit bit patterns passed as i32 arguments.
Both comparisons are signed 32-bit comparisons: return lo if x is below lo; otherwise return hi if x is above hi; otherwise return x.
The chosen input is returned unchanged as a 32-bit pattern; there is no arithmetic here to wrap.

Returns additionally guarantees that the module can be instantiated and that, for every host behavior and every fresh instance, the call terminates without trapping and returns exactly the specified value.
caveats: The bounds are not checked or reordered: the guarantee is the nested signed comparison rule as written, even when the lower bound exceeds the upper bound.
This does not guarantee any additional memory effects or behavior for other exports.
